title: Evaluation of concatenated CNF formulas
statement: Let $\psi_1, \dots, \psi_k$ be CNF formulas over the variables $\{1, \dots, n\}$, and form the single CNF formula obtained by concatenating all of their clause lists into one. Then for every assignment $x \colon \{1,\dots,n\} \to \{\text{true},\text{false}\}$, this concatenated formula evaluates to true at $x$ if and only if every $\psi_i$ evaluates to true at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: a finite list of CNF formulas over n variables
an assignment x of the n variables
replaced:
For any input $x$, the value of the concatenated CNF at $x$ equals the conjunction over
all $\psi$ in the list of $\psi.\mathrm{eval}\,x$; that is, it holds iff every component
CNF holds at $x$.
